subject: VelociMart hosting path — finalization request and quick pilot options
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Aja Patel <aja@velocimart.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@velocimart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-12T22:02:00Z
Subject: VelociMart hosting path — post-demo recap & ask

Hi Aja / Tom — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the two asks we need to finalize recommended hosting:

Summary from the call
- Primary goal: embed contextual product search + personalized rankings in checkout flows.
- Latency targets: p95 inference < 150ms for cart-affecting calls; p95 < 200ms for lower-priority async routes.
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~120 QPS, expected peak bursts up to 450 QPS (short spikes around promotions).
- Data / compliance: VelociMart is PCI scope for payment flows; SOC 2 is a must.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement wants a predictable monthly commitment for next 12 months.

Three hosting options we discussed
1) Hosted API (fastest pilot): fully-managed, lowest up-front cost. Good for functional validation and smaller steady traffic. Predictable for low volume but can have cross-tenant cold-start variance.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, isolation, and easier latency SLOs during peaks. Better for sustained QPS and strict p95 SLAs.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): strongest compliance isolation and network control — typically used when customers require dedicated network boundaries or specific KMS/HSM integration.

Our recommendation and why (short)
- If your primary blocker is speed-to-market and validating model behavior, start with a short Hosted pilot (2–4 weeks) instrumented with tracing and prefix caching.
- If you need hard latency guarantees for checkout calls (p95 <150ms) and predictable cost for peaks, we recommend a Reserved Dedicated path with a small initial commit and an autoscale buffer.
- For PCI-scoped traffic touching payment tokens we should plan for a Dedicated or Private VPC design (we need procurement/legal input).

Asks (what we need from you)
1) Confirm whether checkout inference (the ones that touch product selection at payment time) must be in-scope for your PCI environment.
2) Pick the pilot preference: 
   - "Hosted pilot" to validate correctness and tokenization/logging (lower cost)
   - "Dedicated pilot" if you want us to size for p95 <150ms from day 1
3) If Dedicated is preferred, confirm a target committed QPS (e.g., 200 steady / 450 burst) so we can size nodes.

Attachments: I attached the QPS profile you shared during the call (velocimart_qps_profile.csv) and a draft SOW we can iterate on.

Next steps: if you confirm pilot choice by EOD Friday (2028-09-15) we can schedule a 30-minute benchmark window next week and provide a committed-capacity estimate.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: VelociMart hosting path — post-demo recap & ask

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Checkout inference is definitely in-scope for PCI (payments team flagged we need an auditable boundary).
- p95 < 150ms for checkout is our non-negotiable SLA. For other product-search calls p95 < 200ms is acceptable.
- Procurement will need a rough committed monthly cost for budget planning (ballpark is fine).

For pilot preference: we like the idea of a Hosted pilot to validate model outputs quickly, but the payments team will insist we move critical checkout calls to an isolated environment if latency can't be guaranteed.

Can Ben or your solutions team share a quick sizing + ballpark price for a Dedicated configuration that meets p95 < 150ms at 200 steady / 450 burst? That will help procurement sign off.

Thanks,
Aja
Director of Product, VelociMart
aja@velocimart.com

Subject: Re: VelociMart hosting path — post-demo recap & ask

Thanks Aja — this is very helpful and clear. Quick answers and a concrete pilot approach: 

1) PCI + checkout: understood. For strict PCI-scoped calls we recommend either Dedicated capacity with contractual isolation OR Private VPC (depending on whether you need co-located HSM/KMS). Our security team can provide a controls matrix — SOC 2 is standard for Hosted, but PCI often drives Dedicated/Private.

2) Pilot proposal (practical path to minimize risk and speed):
   - Phase 0 (Hosted pilot, 2 weeks): route non-PCI product-search and personalization traffic through Hosted API. This lets us instrument prompt sets, prefix cache behavior, and correctness checks. It will also surface any model-level latency variance.
   - Phase 1 (Dedicated pilot, 2–4 weeks): spin up a small Dedicated pool sized for your steady/burst profile for checkout calls only. Route checkout inference to Dedicated using smart routing; keep non-critical routes on Hosted.

Sizing guidance (initial estimate)
- To hit p95 ≈ 120–150ms for checkout at 200 steady / 450 burst we recommend starting with 2 reserved GPU nodes (A40-class / quantized runtime equivalent) with a 20–30% autoscale buffer. That should be enough for your burst profile given typical token lengths (~60 tokens).
- If you need headroom for longer sequences or higher concurrency, we add one more node.

Ben and Priyom — can you confirm these sizing assumptions? Ben, please provide the high-level committed monthly pricing for 2-node reserved + autoscale buffer (ballpark) and a quick note on how long a typical Dedicated spin-up takes for a pilot.

Aja / Tom — I’ll also drop the draft SOW (SOW_draft_v1.pdf) and a HubSpot link to the deal board in case procurement wants that included in the PO. If you’re happy with the path above we’ll schedule a 30–60 minute benchmark window next week (suggest Tue 2028-09-19 or Wed 2028-09-20).

Evelyn / Markus — quick internal note to capture numbers we can share with procurement: 
- Baseline Dedicated estimate for 2 reserved nodes (sized as discussed): $22,500 / month committed (covers reserved capacity + support).
- Autoscale buffer (to cover short 450 QPS bursts): add ~20% variable usage; typical overage billing applies beyond commit.
- Pilot Dedicated start time: we can have nodes available within 48–72 hours after contract signature and environment config.

I attached a compact capacity sheet with the math (capacity_estimate_velocimart.xlsx). If they prefer a lower starting commit we can propose 1 reserved node + higher autoscale to reduce monthly commitment but that will increase burst p95 risk.
